ai.description: This lizard reaches 20 cm in total length. It is olive-brown with a distinct dark, arrow-shaped vertebral stripe and a prominent, serrated nuchal crest.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura sagittifera* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, arrow-shaped mark on the throat, which is absent in other similar Indian agamid species.
ai.habitat: The Burmese Japalure inhabits humid subtropical broadleaf forests and montane regions, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters in Northeast India.
ai.behavior: The Burmese Japalure is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks to ambush passing insects while relying on its cryptic coloration for camouflage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura sagittifera* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in Northeast India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Japalura sagittifera* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting high-elevation forests between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
